newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Shell sees 3,000T/day exports from plant.
newsitem.headline: Shell sees 3,000T/day exports from plant.

text.p: Shell Refining Co Bhd plans to export 3,000 tonnes of propylene daily to Asian countries from a 1.0 billion ringgit plant to be built in Malaysia, the Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.

Shell's Long Residue Catalytic Cracking complex will be operational in mid-1999, the national news agency qouted Megat Zaharuddin Megat Nor, local chairman and chief executive officer for the Anglo-Dutch Shell, as saying.

Shell was negotiating with several parties to market the estimated 3,000 tonnes of propylene to be produced daily at the plant, Megat Zaharuddin said at a ground-breaking ceremony for the project in the southwestern town of Port Dickson.
He did not identify the potential Asian clients for the product.
Megat Zaharuddin said all necessary approvals for the project had been obtained and construction would start as scheduled in May 1997.
He said the plant will help raise Shell's refining capacity for crude in Malaysia to 150,000 barrels per day from 105,000 barrels.

The main refined products will be automotive fuels, liquefied petroleum gas and propylene, Megat Zaharuddin said. He added that the new plant's aims include utilising up to 29 percent of a barrel for petrol compared to 19 percent previously.

A multi-product pipeline will also be built to supply jet fuel and other petroluem products from the plant to the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport and areas around the Malaysian capital, he said.
